mandatoryFindings.title: Failure projection discards a successfully read self PID
mandatoryFindings.requirement: Failure/HOLD preserves every known bounded PID; missing starts/fingerprints/image/time remain null. Every actual known helper/client ID must remain available for typed finite history.
mandatoryFindings.evidence: In body-invalid-parent, fake getpid returns9000 and fake getppid returnsNone; joint validation resets both toNone. In bootstrap-integrity-and-parent-failure, fake getpid returns9000 and getppid raises; tuple assignment never stores9000. Both closed HOLD records serialize pid:null. The wrong-valid-parent control preserves9000/3748 and the positive verified-body control returns metadata-only0.
mandatoryFindings.impact: A later missing/invalid parent value loses already acquired numeric lineage, preventing complete future helper-number accounting despite the successful self-PID acquisition. This is a source counterexample, not an actual process observation.
mandatoryFindings.requiredCorrection: Acquire, validate and retain each bounded PID independently and immediately. A parent read/value failure must not clear a valid known self PID (or another independently known bounded ID). Keep HOLD1 and all unknown/qualified fields unchanged. Rebind the body SHA, bootstrap literal, embedded Bash and design/manifest pins coherently.
mandatoryFindings.proof: fake.stdout: body-invalid-parent and bootstrap-integrity-and-parent-failure; fake_cases.py runs only fake os/sys in the same compiled namespace under persistent deny audit.
